To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a single test to assay ACs can be performed by highly diluted prothormbin time (dFiixPT) or by highly diluted Fiix prothrombin (dPT) and the dFiixPT is more sensitive to target specific anticoagents and warfarin than the dPT.
the highly diluted prothormbin time (dProT) or highly diluted factor Xa‐activated partial thromboplastin time (dFiixPT) can be used to assay different anticoagulation drugs in plasma.
the highly diluted PT or highly diluted FiIx‐PT can be used to assay warfarins, dabigatrans, rivaroxabans, apixabans, heparins, and enoxaprins in a single test.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new method to assay anticoagulents and warfarin.
the development of a single test to assay different ACs in plasma.
the use of dFiix‐ or dPT to assay different ACs in plasma.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the dPT and dFiix‐ PT assays are useful in the emergent setting, and the latter assay is more accurate and sensitive than the former.
dFiix‐ and dPT‐based tests can be used to assay different anticoagulant types and warfarin.
the dFiixPT assay is a simple, rapid, and reliable method for assaying ACs in plasma.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
dFiix‐ PT is a better test for the quantification of different ACs than the dPT.
the dFiixPT is superior to the dPT in terms of assay sensitivity, accuracy and precision.
the dFiixPT assay is a useful tool in clinical practice.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the dPT is an effective assay of warfarin antithrombotic effect and that the dFiixPT is a useful test to assay warfurin anticoagulant activity, target specific oral anticoagulans and unfractionated heprain.
